source: Ethical Hacking Academy practical competency standards — internal instructional rubric, not professional certification
guidance: These are portfolio and instructor-assessment criteria. Completing the checklist or a browser simulation alone never proves real-device competency.
criticalRules: No access to third-party devices or networks without specific authorization.
Synthetic records must be explicitly labeled synthetic.
Never submit passwords, access tokens, private logs or identifying data.
Critical safety or scope breaches require remediation regardless of score.
rubric: Commands, reasoning and expected outcomes are technically correct and scoped.
Actual output or labeled synthetic records, timestamps and provenance support conclusions.
Separates observations from hypotheses, alternatives and unknowns.
Permission, privacy, boundaries and stop conditions are respected.
Defines and performs permitted positive/negative tests and a recovery plan.

levels.title: Computer and IT Fundamentals
levels.environment: Academy browser simulator or an owned computer
levels.objective: Locate, inspect, and preserve a harmless test file; distinguish simulated commands from a real shell.
tasks: Paths and files
Create an example.txt in an isolated practice folder. Record the absolute path and relative path. Use Get-Location/Get-Item in PowerShell or pwd/ls -l on Linux; explain which path each command reads.
A path table, two redacted command outputs and a note about where the commands really ran.
Integrity check
Compute a SHA-256 digest on the file, copy it, edit the copy and compute its digest again. On Windows use Get-FileHash; on Linux use sha256sum.
Before/after digests and an explanation of why hashes establish byte equality rather than safety.
System observation
Identify OS release and current username using a native settings screen or read-only commands, separating user identity from administrator privileges.
Redacted host facts, observed permission limits and one safe troubleshooting hypothesis.
levels.failure: Claiming a simulator command operated on the real machine, altering source evidence, or making claims unsupported by hashes.

levels.title: PC Building, Hardware and Repair
levels.environment: Manufacturer diagrams and an unplugged, owned desktop; no PSU enclosure opening
levels.objective: Explain hardware compatibility and carry out a defensible no-power diagnostic sequence.
tasks: Power connectors
Label ATX 24-pin, EPS CPU, PCIe GPU, SATA power and front-panel headers using exact motherboard and PSU manuals; distinguish similar plug shapes.
Annotated diagram with source documentation and a no-force connection checklist.
Memory and POST
Given a DRAM status light, explain a powered-off DIMM seating/slot-compatibility check and compare initial and repeat POST results; simulate if hardware is unavailable.
Step sequence, safety stop conditions, expected observations and what they do not prove.
Upgrade choice
Prepare an under-budget comparison of used workstations by CPU virtualization support, RAM slots, storage, PSU constraints and expansion.
Comparison table, known unknowns, and documented upgrade plan without unsupported performance promises.
levels.failure: Opening a sealed power supply, hot-reseating components, forcing cables or presenting a diagram as proof of real hardware proficiency.

levels.title: System and Network Administration
levels.environment: Owned Windows/Linux systems or isolated VMs; simulation permitted but labeled
levels.objective: Separate process, port, routing and DNS evidence to diagnose a benign service failure.
tasks: Windows baseline
In PowerShell inspect Get-Process, Get-Service and Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem. Explain that the CPU field is cumulative process time, not instantaneous CPU percentage.
Command/output table with timestamps, process ownership and a safe next test.
Linux service
In a test VM inspect systemctl status, journalctl -u and ss -ltn for a known disposable service. Contrast service status with bound interface and port.
Three observations, one plausible alternative explanation and a non-destructive verification plan.
Network diagnosis
Use ipconfig /all or ip addr, then nslookup or dig for an owned/test hostname. Explain the distinction between DNS failure, route failure and application response.
Network diagram, anonymized responses, interpretation and evidence limits.
levels.failure: Restarting or changing an unrelated production service, treating one ping as proof of full connectivity, or probing unapproved targets.

levels.title: Cybersecurity Foundations
levels.environment: Fictional organizational records and Academy security simulations
levels.objective: Interpret identity, access and event records while maintaining privacy and uncertainty.
tasks: Access review
Build a matrix for employee, help desk, administrator and service identities; contrast assigned group membership with approved job duties.
Least-privilege matrix, two overgrant findings, approval owner and negative test.
Event timeline
Normalize mixed UTC and local-time log events; mark duplicate records and gaps. Do not infer attacker identity from failed login alone.
Source-provenance timeline including uncertainty and confidence for each conclusion.
Recovery readiness
Define a recovery point objective and a recovery time objective for a fictional internal service; specify a restore test.
Recovery criteria, data-loss estimate and an independently verifiable acceptance test.
levels.failure: Confusing authentication with authorization, publishing real tokens, or reporting a hypothetical attack as confirmed.

levels.title: Ethical Hacking and Authorized Assessment
levels.environment: Academy simulations or explicitly approved isolated test targets only
levels.objective: Create and execute a safe assessment plan that is bounded by written authorization.
tasks: Written scope
Define target names, allowed techniques, dates, stop conditions and escalation contacts for a fictional exercise. Exclude all other hosts.
Signed/fictional authorization record and a clear stop/go table.
Reproducible finding
Use a synthetic access-denied or web error example to record exact observations, permitted verification and likely business impact without claiming real exploitation.
Evidence log, impact assumptions, reproducible steps and fix criteria.
Retest and reporting
Describe positive and negative tests of a corrected access-control rule and write a concise executive decision note.
Retest criteria, owner, uncertainty statement and executive summary.
levels.failure: Touching targets outside approved scope, inventing access to production data, or presenting a simulation as a live compromise.

levels.title: Home Labs, Servers and Virtualization
levels.environment: Isolated owned virtual network, or diagrams/browser simulation until hardware is available
levels.objective: Build or design an isolated two-system lab with recoverable configuration.
tasks: Isolation design
Diagram a host-only or internal virtual switch with a client and disposable service VM. Explain why bridged mode can expose vulnerable guests to household networks.
Network adapter inventory and expected allowed/denied paths.
Boundary validation
Where hardware allows, use connectivity tests strictly between owned guests and verify disallowed routes toward household devices remain unavailable.
Test matrix with source, destination, expected result, observed result and uncertainty.
Recovery rehearsal
Restore an approved snapshot and check OS, test account, service listener and network conditions; distinguish a snapshot from an off-host backup.
Restoration log, previous state, actual evidence and failure/rollback limits.
levels.failure: Connecting intentionally vulnerable practice guests to family devices, claiming isolation from a private IP alone or assuming a snapshot is a verified backup.

levels.title: Advanced Red Team Operations
levels.environment: Synthetic corporate engagement and intentionally isolated owned training assets
levels.objective: Perform evidence-led, legally bounded adversary-emulation planning and defender coordination.
tasks: Engagement design
Write an objective, fictional threat assumptions, allowed actions, target exclusions, emergency halt and defender notification plan.
Rules of engagement, authorization and escalation triggers.
Detection hypothesis
Using synthetic proxy and login logs, formulate two falsifiable hypotheses and two read-only or simulated verification steps.
Timeline linking evidence to each hypothesis, with explicit alternatives.
Executive report
Prioritize risk using evidence quality, impact, exposure, controls and uncertainty; include one remediation and retest per issue.
A board-readable summary, technical appendix and action owner.
levels.failure: Claiming real-world compromise based on synthetic records, using production credentials or bypassing documented scope.

levels.title: Professional Capstone and Mastery
levels.environment: Integrated Academy synthetic corporation plus optional owned isolated lab
levels.objective: Demonstrate independent end-to-end evidence collection, judgment, reporting and remediation validation.
tasks: Integrated case
Receive an unfamiliar simulated change/incident scenario and establish a baseline, evidence preservation and scoped triage.
Source-aware evidence ledger, assumptions and decision timeline.
Defensible response
Choose a least-disruptive, authorized corrective action and test both expected success and expected denial after the change.
Change plan, reversible steps and before/after acceptance results.
Oral/written defense
Explain uncertainty, distinguish lab demonstration from real device skill, and defend a recovery and security decision to a mock reviewer.
Technical report, executive note, critical limitations and remediation plan.
levels.failure: Missing provenance, unsupported certainty, absent retest evidence, breached authority or misrepresenting simulated work as real equipment qualification.
